Piecewise-exponential (Poisson-trick) Bayesian PH model -> psurv.

Source: R/psurv.R
psurv_from_pwexp.Rd

A genuine Bayesian proportional-hazards analogue with a piecewise-constant baseline hazard, fit WITHOUT Stan: split the follow-up at cut points into person-time pieces, fit a Poisson GLM with piece-specific intercepts (the log baseline hazards) and covariate log-HRs, and draw the posterior from the GLM's Laplace approximation N(coef, vcov). This is the plan's robustness comparator (B1) and shows the framework is model-agnostic — it produces the identical psurv object as stan_surv or the Cox-Laplace fallback, so B2-B6 are unchanged. Needs only the survival package.

Usage

psurv_from_pwexp(
  formula,
  data,
  horizons,
  cuts = NULL,
  n_pieces = 8L,
  S = 500L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

formula

Surv(time, status) ~ covariates.

data

the data.frame.

horizons

numeric[H] evaluation horizons.

cuts

interior cut points; NULL => event-time quantiles giving n_pieces pieces.

n_pieces

number of baseline-hazard pieces when cuts is NULL.

S, seed

posterior draws and RNG seed.
